Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.vpn

Class ReconnectPolicy

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.vpn.ReconnectPolicy
public final class ReconnectPolicy extends Object
The pure auto-reconnect backoff policy. When a tunnel that was up drops unexpectedly and its profile is marked auto-connect, VpnPanel retries the connection on a schedule derived here: an exponential backoff (each attempt waits twice the previous) clamped to a ceiling, with a hard cap on the number of attempts so a permanently-down gateway cannot spin forever.

Every method is pure and side-effect free - the panel owns the timer and the actual reconnect, this class only decides whether to retry and how long to wait - so the whole schedule is unit-testable headless with no clock, no thread and no tunnel.

  • Constructor Details

    • ReconnectPolicy

      public ReconnectPolicy(long initialDelayMs, long maxDelayMs, int maxAttempts)
      Builds a policy, normalising nonsense inputs so a hand-tuned policy can never produce a negative delay or an infinite retry loop.
      Parameters:
      initialDelayMs - the delay before the first retry (negatives clamp to 0)
      maxDelayMs - the delay ceiling (clamped up to at least the initial)
      maxAttempts - the retry cap (negatives clamp to 0 - never retry)

  • Method Details

    • defaultPolicy

      public static ReconnectPolicy defaultPolicy()
      The default policy: 2 s initial, doubling to a 60 s ceiling, 5 attempts.

    • delayForAttempt

      public long delayForAttempt(int attempt)
      The delay before the given (1-based) attempt: the initial delay for the first, doubling each attempt thereafter and never exceeding the ceiling. Overflow-safe - once the doubling would pass the ceiling (or wrap) it returns the ceiling.
      Parameters:
      attempt - the 1-based attempt number (values < 1 are treated as 1)
      Returns:
      the delay in milliseconds, never negative

    • shouldRetry

      public boolean shouldRetry(int attemptsMade)
      Whether another attempt is allowed once attemptsMade have already been made. A negative count is treated as "no attempts made" but never retried, so a corrupted counter cannot loop.
      Parameters:
      attemptsMade - the number of attempts already made (0-based)
      Returns:
      true while 0 <= attemptsMade < maxAttempts
